sentences.text: The petitioners are the accused in C.P.No.103/2017 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Adoor.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Adoor
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The above case arose out of a private complaint filed by the de facto complainant alleging the commission of offence under Sections 192, 366, 376, 379, 420, 423, 465,
466, 468 & 294(b) read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

The learned Magistrate proceeded with the enquiry under Sections 200 & 202 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, and found that there are sufficient grounds to proceed against the petitioners for the commission of the aforesaid offences.

Accordingly, the complaint was taken on file and summons ordered to the petitioners/accused as per order dated 09.06.2017 in C.M.P.No.4225/2015.
2.
In the present petition, the petitioners would contend that they are falsely implicated in the crime.

It is further stated that the issue has been amicably settled with the de facto complainant/
second respondent.
The petitioners seek an order quashing the proceedings in C.P. No. 103/2015 since the second respondent is said to be having no grievances against them at present.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.
The affidavit filed by the de facto complainant/ second respondent expressing her willingness to quash the proceedings against the petitioners, is placed on record as Annexure-3.

It is stated by the second respondent in Annexure-3 affidavit that she was having an affair with the first petitioner and that they resided in Delhi during the year 2015 pursuant to her elopement with the first petitioner.
It is further stated that they surrendered before Pandalam Police and were produced before this Court.
The de facto complainant was thereafter sent along with the first petitioner.
In the affidavit, the de facto complainant has also stated that she preferred the complaint against the petitioners due to some disputes which arose in the family.
5. The affidavit filed by the de facto complainant in the above regard would reveal that none of the offences as alleged by her in the complaint had actually taken place.
Therefore, the prayer of the petitioners to quash the proceedings against them, is well founded.
In the result, the petition stands allowed.
The proceedings against the petitioners/accused in C.P.No.103/2017 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Adoor, are hereby quashed.
